course_name_original: Cálculo y Diseño de Máquinas I
prerequisites: Having completed Elasticity and Strength of Materials

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the necessary theoretical and practical knowledge for the calculation and design of machines.
Know the basic compositions of machines and mechanisms.
Understand dynamic considerations in mechanical design.
Calculate the fatigue of parts by various methods.
Design and calculate joining elements, wedges, keys, and pins.
Know the types of screws and calculate power screws.
Understand how to analyze shaft support systems based on rolling bearings.
Know and calculate the belt-pulley transmission system.
Know and design spur gear transmission systems.
Develop the ability to solve problems and make decisions in design.

syllabus_topics: Dynamic considerations in mechanical design. FATIGUE.
Stages of the fatigue failure process.
Design effects. Practical recommendations for fatigue design.
General concepts, classification: Rigid, flexible, universal joints, and clutches.
Screws for mechanical joints and mechanical displacements.
Common denominations according to screw use.
MODULE IV. Project to be carried out, consisting of the design of a shaft subjected to various forces, according to transmission elements. Problem solving in groups and individually.
Activities to be developed in another language
Problems in English with exercises from the different topics.

assessment_methods.method: Multiple-choice test and short exercise solving during the course
Individual problem solving during the course (in-class and submitted)
Development test during the official exam period

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on continuous assessment, which includes three in-person tests (90%) and various activities (10%). The first development test counts for 30%, a combined multiple-choice test and short exercises for 10%, and the final development test (during the official exam period) for 50%. A minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required for each development test and the multiple-choice test. Attendance and passing (APTA) the mandatory laboratory practices are also required to pass the course. If practices are not passed, students must take a practice exam during the official exam period. If minimum requirements are not met, the final grade will be 4 in the transcript, even if the weighted average is 5.0 or higher. For single evaluation, a single development test accounts for 100% of the grade, along with passing practices.
